Arizona Cardinals.longComment: The Cardinals were already preparing for Josh Johnson to operate as the starting quarterback Sunday, as Beck entered the weekend with the questionable tag due to back spasms. Joey Aguilar will operate as Johnson's backup, and Beck's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Commanders on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Gaines will miss a fourth consecutive game while recovering from an ankle injury, and his next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Commanders on Sunday, Nov. 29. Hjalte Froholdt has cleared the league's concussion protocol and is slated to start at center against Kansas City.

Carter opened the regular season on injured reserve due to a knee injury he picked up in training camp in early August. He logged a trio of full practices during Week 11 prep but is not quite ready to return, so his next chance to make his 2026 debut is Week 12 against the Commanders on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Conner hasn't played in a game since Week 3 of last season, when he sustained a right foot/ankle injury that required surgery. Though he was able to participate in individual drills in training camp, he never advanced to team work before being placed on injured reserve with a designation to return Aug. 30. The Cardinals still haven't cleared Conner to practice nearly three months later, which suggests that he either experienced a setback over the summer or plateaued in his recovery. Whatever the case, Conner doesn't seem close to a return, and the chances of him playing at any point this season will grow dimmer with each week that he doesn't practice.

Though the procedure will bring an end to Minshew's season, he's expected to make a full recovery ahead of the 2027 campaign. The veteran quarterback sustained the injury while making his lone start of the season Week 9 in Seattle, but he played though the elbow issue and completed 21 of 30 passes for 166 yards. Rookie third-round pick Carson Beck took over as the Cardinals' starting quarterback in Week 10 and is expected to lead the offense for the remainder of the season.

This move was a foregone conclusion, as head coach Mike LaFleur said Monday that Burch will miss the remainder of the campaign after suffering an MCL injury to his left knee. The defensive end finished his sophomore NFL season with 19 tackles, including 1.0 sacks, over 10 games. Burch will now look to get healthy in the hope of being ready for the 2027 campaign.

Wingard picked up a wrist injury in the team's 34-6 loss to the Rams in Week 10, and he will now be forced to miss at least four contests while recovering from the injury. In Wingard's absence, Kitan Crawford and Dadrion Taylor-Demerson are both candidates to replace him as the team's starting free safety Sunday versus the Chiefs.

Baltimore Ravens.longComment: Hawkins was a limited participant throughout the practice week, but it isn't enough for him to return in Week 11. The 29-year-old will miss his fifth straight game due to a knee injury. K'Von Wallace will continue to take reps in Hawkins' place.

Madubuike popped up on the injury report as a non-participant in back-to-back practices due to a hamstring injury. With the 29-year-old out, John Jenkins will likely see a higher snap count on defense. Madubuike has 22 tackles (12 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and two pass deflections in eight regular-season games.

Minter noted that after holding "internal conversations," he and the Ravens' brain trust decided to deactivate Humphrey for Week 11. Per Hensley, Humphrey acknowledged after Wednesday's practice that he regretted the comments he made in the podcast and issued an apology, so he's not expected to face any discipline beyond being held out of the matchup with the Panthers. Through the Ravens' first 10 games, Humphrey has tallied 40 tackles, nine pass breakups, two forced fumbles and one fumble recovery.

Last Friday, head coach Jesse Minter announced that Jackson was facing a projected recovery timeline of 6-to-10 weeks after requiring a procedure to address a broken and dislocated thumb. A Week 16 return would be right up against the short end of that timeline, so if Jackson has shown notable improvement by that point, he could push to play if the 4-6 Ravens haven't faded from the playoff picture. While Jackson remains sidelined for at least a few more weeks, the Ravens will entrust trade-deadline acquisition Jacoby Brissett to direct the offense.

Buffalo Bills.longComment: Per Matt Parrino of The Syracuse Post-Standard, Oliver notified the Bills' medical staff Saturday morning of pain in his oblique, but there's still optimism that the veteran defensive lineman will be available for Sunday's AFC East tilt. In the event that Oliver is inactive or operates on a snap count, more playing time on defense would be available for DeWayne Carter, Greg Gaines and Landon Jackson.

Hamlin was held out of practice in each of the first two practices of Week 11 prep due to a toe injury. He put together a limited session Friday to draw the questionable tag, but if he cannot play against the Dolphins, then Jalon Kilgore and Sam Franklin would operate as the Bills' backup safeties behind Amani Hooker and Cole Bishop for Sunday's AFC East tilt.

Hawes' practice reps during Week 11 prep were limited by a shoulder injury, which he may have picked up during the Bills' Week 10 win over the Jets. Dalton Kincaid (thumb) is listed as doubtful, so that leaves Dawson Knox and Keleki Latu as the two healthy tight ends on the Bills' 53-man roster heading into the weekend. If Hawes is cleared to play, then he would operate as the TE2 behind Knox in the event that Kincaid is inactive.

Williams missed the last three practices with a calf injury he sustained in Week 10 against the Jets. The 25-year-old is set to miss his first game since Week 5 of the 2025 regular season.  Kaleb Elarms-Orr should be in line to start in place of Williams, alongside Terrel Bernard.

Benford missed a trio of practices ahead of Week 11 after exiting early against the Jets with a groin injury. Sunday's game against the Dolphins marks the 26-year-old's second miss of the season. He has 33 tackles (23 solo) and eight pass deflections through eight regular-season appearances.

The Bills are massive 16.5-point favorites at home against a Dolphins team missing its starting quarterback, so it presents an opportunity to give Kincaid a rest after he's been playing through injuries the last several weeks. Dawson Knox will remain an every-down tight end, with Jackson Hawes and Keleki Latu stepping into elevated spots. The biggest beneficiaries likely will be DJ Moore and Khalil Shakir in terms of target opportunities, though Buffalo should run all over this Miami defense.

It's not immediately clear when he suffered the back injury, but Reed-Adams will now have to sit out at least four games as he recovers. His absence leaves veteran Austin Corbett as Buffalo's undisputed backup plan at guard behind starters Alec Anderson and O'Cyrus Torrence.

Carolina Panthers.longComment: Brooks was a full practice participant in all three sessions during Week 11 prep. However, the third-year running back is not quite ready to be activated from injured reserve, and he's slated to miss his eighth consecutive game while recovering from a groin injury. Trevor Etienne, Anthony Tyus and AJ Dillon will continue to operate as the Panthers' backfield depth options behind Chuba Hubbard in the absence of Brooks, whose next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Buccaneers on Monday, Nov. 30.

Simmons did not participate in Week 11 prep due to a knee injury he likely sustained in the Panthers' Week 10 win over the Saints. The reserve free safety plays primarily on special teams, logging six snaps on defense and 206 on special teams this season.

Tremble put together a DNP-LP-LP practice log during Week 11 prep while managing a knee injury that he picked up during the Panthers' 20-17 win over the Saints in Week 10. Darren Waller (knee) also is listed as questionable, which leaves Mitchell Evans, Feleipe Franks and Ja'Tavion Sanders as the Panthers' healthy tight ends on the 53-man roster heading into the weekend. Tremble's status for Sunday's game may not officially be known until 90 minutes before the 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff, when Carolina announces its list of inactive players.

Jackson remains on injured reserve, but he logged three straight full practices ahead of Week 11, earning him the questionable tag. The 29-year-old hasn't played since Week 3, when he exited early with a groin injury. The Panthers would have to activate Jackson at some point Saturday for him to be eligible to suit up Sunday.
Okereke hasn't practiced all week and will miss his third straight game due to a foot injury likely suffered in Week 8. Tyrel Dodson is slated to get another start.

According to Person, Waller told coach Dave Canales he's ready to play Sunday against Baltimore, so fantasy players should proceed as if Waller will be active. Waller's production has been all over the place this season, making him difficult to pin down as a reliable weekly fantasy option. He's more of a best-ball type of fantasy asset.

Christensen drew the questionable tag for Sunday's game against the Saints after logging a trio of full practices. However, he's not quite ready to return from a hamstring injury, and his next chance to suit up is Week 11 against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 22.

Chicago Bears.longComment: Gordon did not participate in practice coming off the Bears' bye week after picking up a shoulder injury in the team's Week 9 game against the Buccaneers. Week 11 marks the sixth game the 26-year-old has missed this season. Malik Muhammad, who is coming back from a toe injury, is expected to see more reps in Gordon's place.

Thomas appears to have picked up an injury in the Bears' lead-up to Week 11, as he did not participate in Friday's practice. The rookie third-rounder acts as the team's top kick-return option. Should he not play, Josh Blackwell may take over duties on special teams.
Scott will be required to miss at least the next four games. He's appeared in four contests this season, playing 65 snaps on special teams.

Street was injured in Monday night's win over the Seahawks and had to be carted to the locker room. He's now expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 season. Fellow DT Grady Jarrett (groin) was also injured in Seattle, making the move for Jeffery Simmons that much more important for Chicago.

Cincinnati Bengals.longComment: Burks has been working through a groin issue for the past couple of weeks, and he aggravated the injury during the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday. His placement on IR means he'll be required to miss at least the next four games, so his next opportunity to play is Week 15 against the Panthers on Sunday, Dec. 20.

The linebacker suffered a broken forearm in Week 5 against the Dolphins but now has a maximum of 21 days to get ready for a return to action. He played just one defensive snap across the first four games of the season but was a fixture on special teams.

The cornerback played on 82 percent of the defensive snaps last week against Pittsburgh and has yet to miss a game this season. Hill does have an extra day to get over this illness, as the Bengals don't play until Monday night against the Commanders.

Iosivas had his 21-day practice window opened last week but remains on injured reserve. With Dohnte Meyers playing well as the Bengals' WR3, there's likely no rush to activate Iosivas, who has just 87 career regular-season catches across 52 appearances. He's averaged 20.2 receiving yards per game in his career.

Cleveland Browns.longComment: Burton was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Texans due to a calf injury that he picked up against the Saints in Week 9. The injury is severe enough for him to warrant an extended absence, and since he's now on IR, Burton will be required to miss at least four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 15 against the Giants on Sunday, Dec. 20. Since the Browns do not have another fullback on the 53-man roster, the team will likely turn to tight ends Carsen Ryan, Zaire Mitchell-Paden and Blake Whiteheart to provide blocking out of the backfield, per Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com.

Dallas Cowboys.longComment: Locke was unable to practice all week while in the league's concussion protocol, and his absence means Markquese Bell will likely start alongside Malik Hooker at safety Sunday. Locke's next chance to play is Week 12 against the Eagles on Thanksgiving Day.

Thompson ended Week 11 prep with back-to-back full practices, but he would need to be activated from injured reserve in order to be available for Sunday's contest. The veteran safety has missed the Cowboys' last seven games while recovering from a hamstring injury that he sustained against the Ravens in Week 3. Thompson's return would be timely, seeing as P.J. Locke (concussion) has already been ruled out.

Schoonmaker was held out of practice Thursday and Friday due to an illness, and he's drawn the questionable tag heading into the weekend. Jake Ferguson (knee) has already been ruled out, and with Schoonmaker under the weather, that leaves Brevyn Spann-Ford and James Mitchell as the Cowboys' two healthy tight ends on the 53-man roster ahead of Sunday's contest. Michael Trigg could be elevated from the practice squad to the active roster depending on Schoonmaker's recovery.

It will be the second game that Mingo will miss while recovering from foot and ankle injuries, which have prevented him from practicing over the last two weeks, and his next chance to suit up is Week 12 against the Eagles on Thanksgiving Day. In Mingo's absence, KaVontae Turpin and Camden Brown will be the Cowboys' rotational options at wide receiver behind CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and Ryan Flournoy.

Ferguson injured his knee in a Week 9 win over the Colts, while the ankle issue is more of a lingering concern after he initially sustained a low sprain in a Week 8 loss to the Cardinals. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer previously announced Nov. 9 that Ferguson was set to miss multiple weeks, so the tight end's continued absence from practice comes as little surprise. In Ferguson's stead, Brevyn Spann-Ford should be in line for another turn as Dallas' top tight end in Week 11.

Booker is expected to miss multiple weeks after injuring his ankle in the first half of Sunday's game against the 49ers, per Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com. The 22-year-old may be able to avoid being placed on injured reserve with the Cowboys' bye coming in Week 14. T.J. Bass will likely slot into Booker's right guard spot.

Denver Broncos.longComment: The Broncos opened Lohner's 21-day practice window Wednesday. The tight end is not quite ready to make his season debut, as he is still tending to his recovery from a foot injury he sustained in the offseason. Lohner was a full participant in all three Week 11 prep sessions, meaning his odds of returning in Week 12 are quite good if he can continue to log full sessions.

Jones strung together three limited practices Week 11 prep, and he has a chance to return from a one-game absence due to a hamstring injury that he picked up in Week 8 against the Chiefs. JL Skinner figures to be the top candidate to start alongside Talanoa Hufanga at safety if Jones is not cleared to play against Las Vegas.

Uwazurike wasn't able to practice at all this week due to a shoulder issue. He started seven of Denver's first eight games, but he's now required to miss the team's next four contests. Third-round rookie Tyler Onyedim could see the first gameday action of his career as a result.

Detroit Lions.longComment: Reed was a limited participant in all three practices during Week 11 prep while tending to a hip injury, which has prevented him from playing in each of the Lions' last two games. Per Jeremy  Reisman of PrideofDetroit.com on Wednesday, Reed did not express optimism that he would face Tampa Bay. Khalil Dorsey (ankle) and Ennis Rakestraw (shoulder) are both also listed as questionable, which leaves Rock Ya-Sin, Roger McCreary and Christian Izien as the only healthy cornerbacks on the Lions' 53-man roster heading into the weekend.

If Vaki is unable to play against Tampa Bay, Jacob Saylors would move up to RB2 status, but Jahmyr Gibbs would have a chance to see an even bigger share of the backfield opportunities in that scenario.

Hutchinson's move to IR was merely a formality after he was diagnosed with a torn ACL in his right knee following his early exit from this past Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munich. The No. 2 overall pick in the 2022 NFL Draft has now succumbed to two season-ending injuries through his first five years in the league, after a fractured tibia and fibula in his left leg cut short his 2024 campaign.

Green Bay Packers.longComment: Head coach Matt LaFleur didn't sound optimistic about Jacobs' chances of playing against the Rams on Wednesday, but the veteran running back will "have a chance to prove" that he can suit up for that contest over the next few days at practice, per Matt Schneidman of The Athletic. Weston Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site relayed that Jacobs was spotted at Saturday's practice with a "claw-like cast" on his fingers. In the event that Jacobs doesn't play Wednesday, the Packers would enter the game with a backfield of Kaleb Johnson, MarShawn Lloyd and Chris Brooks.

Parsons is in the final stages of his recovery from a torn ACL in his left knee that he sustained in December of 2025. He's been limited in practice since being designated to return from injured reserve Nov. 4, and a full session over the coming days should be enough for Parsons to make his 2026 debut. He will likely operate under a snap count once he's cleared to return, but his availability would also impact the workload of both Lukas Van Ness and Barryn Sorrell.

Cisse did not return to Sunday's contest after exiting the game during the first quarter with a rib injury. Coach Matt LaFleur says the cornerback is "fine," and it appears Cisse will return to practice after the Packers' Week 11 bye.

The Packers' decision to rule Moore out with an ankle injury in the Week 10 loss to the Vikings was a precautionary move after the 26-year-old made his first appearance since returning from injured reserve. It's unclear if the fifth-year pro will be sidelined for any coming games, but Savion Williams and Matthew Golden will likely act as primary return options if Moore misses any time.

Melton exited Sunday's game because of a thigh injury, and he will not be cleared to return to the contest. Skyy Moore (ankle) will also not return, so Savion Williams and Matthew Golden will operate as the top return options on kickoffs and punts.

Houston Texans.longComment: The wideout had one of his more productive games of the season before being injured, as he caught both of his targets for 40 yards and a touchdown. His 40 yards were the second-most he's produced in a game this season. Boutte is up to 21 grabs for 359 yards and three touchdowns on 31 targets across 10 games in 2026.

The Texans announced Rutledge's injury in the waning moments of the contest, but he had been in the medical tent well before that time. Febechi Nwaiwu took over at left guard following Rutledge's departure. With Houston not set to play again until Sunday, Nov. 29, against Baltimore, Rutledge will look to recover from the stinger in time to suit up.

Rankins sustained an apparent ankle injury during the second quarter of Thursday's contest, and he was able to walk gingerly to the sideline under his own power. In his absence, rookie second-rounder Kayden McDonald figures to see an increase in snaps on the defensive line.

Braswell suffered an injury in kick coverage on the opening kickoff and was promptly carted off the field with his right leg in an air cast, per James Boyd of The Athletic. The Texans will have to try to find a way to replace his production on special teams.

Teller was unavailable in Week 10 against the Browns due to an illness, and he'll be sidelined in Week 11 by a back injury. In his absence, rookie fourth-rounder Febechi Nwaiwu projects as the Texans' top option off the bench at guard.

Indianapolis Colts.longComment: McGowan was injured just before halftime while returning a kickoff. He was deemed questionable to return at the beginning of the third quarter and subsequently was ruled out shortly thereafter. The rookie running back gained seven yards on three carries and caught his only target for one yard before exiting while adding 117 yards on three kickoff returns. Jonathan Taylor should continue to get most of the work at running back for the Colts for the rest of the game, and DJ Giddens should handle whatever backfield snaps that Taylor doesn't get.

The cornerback has a history of calf issues, and the Colts, in the middle of a lost season, have no reason to push Gardner to play on a short week. With Charvarius Ward (knee) also out, Indy is down its top two cornerbacks against a pass-heavy Houston offense.

Jacksonville Jaguars.longComment: Green has strung together six consecutive full practices since being designated to return from injured reserve Nov. 11. He's not quite ready to be activated from IR, so his next chance to play is Week 12 against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 29. Green is in the final stages of his recovery from an elbow injury that he suffered in Week 1 against the Browns.

Striggow entered the league's concussion protocol following the Jaguars' Week 10 win over the Titans. He was limited in all three practice sessions during Week 11 prep, and he would need to pass an evaluation by an independent neurologist in order to clear protocol and be available for Sunday's contest. Bryan Thomas and Wesley Williams would both see a bump in rotational snaps at defensive end if Striggow is inactive.

Jonah Monheim will draw the start at center in place of Hainsey, who exited this past Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans due to a knee sprain, per Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com. According to Fowler, Hainsey's knee injury isn't considered season-ending, but the veteran lineman is viewed as week-to-week and could be a candidate for injured reserve.

Kansas City Chiefs.longComment: Norman-Lott was removed from the reserve/PUP list Wednesday, but he may not be ready to make his 2026 regular-season debut as he continues to work his way back from a torn ACL that he sustained in October of 2025. His return would give the Chiefs more depth on the interior defensive line behind starters Chris Jones and Khyiris Tonga.

Moore will miss a second consecutive game due to an ankle injury, which means Joshua Ezeudu will likely start at right tackle against Arizona. Moore's next chance to play is Week 12 against Buffalo on Thanksgiving Day.

Smith entered the league's concussion protocol during the Chiefs' Week 10 win over the Falcons. He was unable to practice all week, and his absence means Mike Caliendo will likely start at right guard Sunday. Smith's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Bills on Thanksgiving Day.

Walker, who wasn't able to practice this week, will thus target a potential return Thursday against the Bills. The Chiefs -- per ESPN.com -- are "optimistic" he will play Thanksgiving night, but they will err on the side of caution with a short week ahead, and as such Emmett Johnson -- who rushed 22 times for 101 yards and brought in six of seven targets for 70 yards and two touchdowns in Week 10 -- is headed toward a second consecutive start this weekend.

Wiley was carted to the locker room in the first quarter of the Chiefs' Week 10 win over the Falcons with an ankle injury. The tight end will now be on IR as he nurses his fractured ankle until at least the latter part of the regular season. Travis Kelce, Noah Gray and Jake Briningstool are now the only tight ends on the Chiefs' active roster.

Las Vegas Raiders.longComment: Fatukasi was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice before downgrading to a DNP on Thursday. The defensive lineman capped off Week 11 prep with a full session Friday but remains questionable for Sunday's divisional bout. If Fatukasi cannot suit up, the absence of Tonka Hemingway (stinger) means Thomas Booker and Tim Keenan will likely start alongside nose tackle Adam Butler for Sunday's game.

Hemingway did not participate in any Week 11 prep sessions as he continues to deal with a stinger injury he likely suffered in the Raiders' Week 10 loss to the Seahawks. With Hemingway ruled out and Folorunso Fatukasi (toe) listed as questionable, Thomas Booker is currently the only healthy defensive end for the Raiders as they head into a divisional bout.

Bowers, who was limited at Thursday's practice, was back on the field Friday, but the tight end nonetheless will head into the weekend with a questionable designation. Look for added intel regarding his Week 11 status to arrive late Saturday or early Sunday via the usual assortment of NFL insiders, but if Bowers is limited or ends up out for his team's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff, fellow TE Michael Mayer will merit fantasy lineup consideration while facing 7-2 Denver.

Gay, who was limited Wednesday, logged a DNP on Thursday, but it looks like he'll work in some capacity to close out the week. Per Warren, the Raiders worked out three kickers with Gay injured, but it appears as though it's only Gay and practice-squad member Kansei Matsuzawa available to handle kicks at Friday's practice.

Los Angeles Chargers.longComment: Waxter ended Week 11 prep with consecutive limited sessions after being a non-participant Wednesday. If Waxter cannot suit up for Sunday's game, Deane Leonard is set to be the only reserve cornerback behind starters Cam Hart, Donte Jackson and Tarheeb Still (ankle).

Shelley did not participate in any Week 11 prep sessions. The cornerback likely sustained his ankle injury in the Chargers' Week 10 win over the Ravens. In the reserve cornerback's absence, Deane Leonard could see snaps at slot cornerback if Tarheeb Still (ankle) does not suit up for Sunday's game.
Williamson ended Week 11 prep with consecutive DNPs. The strong safety remains sidelined with a calf injury he sustained in Week 8 against the Rams.

Still was added to Friday's practice report as a limited participant due to an ankle injury. His late addition to the injury report isn't a great sign ahead of Sunday's game, and if he's unable to play, then Deane Leonard and Genesis Smith would both be in line for more snaps in the Chargers' secondary.

Henley was unable to practice all week, and head coach Jim Harbaugh said Friday that the fourth-year linebacker has been working through knee soreness since Monday's win against the Ravens, per Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com. Denzel Perryman and Marlowe Wax figure to be the top candidates to start at inside linebacker alongside Del'Shawn Phillips in the absence of Henley, whose next chance to play is Week 12 against the Patriots on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Thompson has been sidelined by a hamstring injury and has not seen regular-season action since Week 2 against the Raiders. If he's ruled out for Sunday's game, then the rookie fourth-rounder's next chance to play would be Week 12 against the Patriots on Sunday, Nov. 29.

The tight end is still in the concussion protocol, so he'll be up against it to clear the final hurdles, especially after the Chargers played Monday night against Baltimore. If Kolar is ruled out, David Njoku and Oronde Gadsden should handle most of the tight-end duties for the Bolts.

McConkey, who didn't record any snaps during Week 9 action due to back spasms and was inactive in Week 10, has been able to practice in a limited fashion thus far this week, but thanks to his official 'questionable' designation, his status will need to be tracked in advance of Sunday's 4:05 ET kickoff. If McConkey is limited or out versus New York, Tre' Harris could maintain a key role in the Chargers' pass-catching corps alongside fellow WR Quentin Johnston.
Taylor is battling an ankle injury and was ruled out for the Week 10 meeting with Baltimore. Now on injured reserve, he will be required to miss at least four games before being eligible to return.

Los Angeles Rams.longComment: Regarding the looming practice status of Adams, who is on IR and last played in Week 6, McVay said Friday, "We're not quite there yet." On the plus side, Beacham relays that the Rams still are hopeful Adams will be ready retake the field next week. The veteran pass-catcher's availability gains added import going forward, following Friday's report from Beacham that fellow starting WR Puka Nacua is on track to miss a couple of months after undergoing an MCL procedure.

Even if Ferguson is moved back to the active roster, coach Sean McVay's comments indicate the tight end still won't be ready to play coming out of the team's Week 11 bye. His activation at least would keep him off season-ending IR, but his near-term availability remains uncertain until the Rams signal he's ready for game action. With Puka Nacua (knee/toe) likely done for the remainder of the regular season following MCL surgery, Ferguson and Davante Adams (hamstring) are needed badly in this offense.

Given that timetable, Nacua -- who already is on injured reserve -- could be out for the rest of the regular season, which is a huge blow to the Rams' pass-catching corps going forward. In Nacua's continued absence, Konata Mumpfield, CJ Daniels, Tutu Atwell and Xavier Smith are the team's healthy options at WR, though fellow starter Davante Adams (hamstring) is believed to be targeting a return in Week 12 following the team's bye.

The starting center is set to miss 4-6 weeks with a hamstring injury. Shelton will likely be placed on injured reserve while he recovers. Dylan McMahon (knee, IR) also sustained an injury in the Rams' Week 10 win over the Cardinals, leaving Beaux Limmer to finish out the contest at center and to likely fill in as the starter for the foreseeable future.

McMahon suffered a knee injury during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday. The injury is severe enough for McMahon to require a stint on IR, so he'll be required to miss at least the next four games, with his next chance to play being Week 16 against the Seahawks on Christmas Day. With Coleman Shelton nursing a hamstring injury, the Rams may have to turn to other options like David Quessenberry or Beaux Limmer to fill in at center for the time being.

Miami Dolphins.longComment: Baker opened the season on the Dolphins' PUP list due to a knee injury. He was a full participant in all three practices during Week 11 prep, and while he's still listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Bills, Baker appears to be in line to make his 2026 regular-season debut. He played in all 17 regular-season games for the Titans in 2025 and finished with 55 tackles (39 solo) and seven pass defenses.

Simpson upgraded to a limited participant in Friday's practice after missing consecutive sessions to start Week 11 prep. The reserve cornerback remains unlikely to suit up, but Friday's partial session gives the 26-year-old a chance to be active on game day.

Pinion did not participate in any Week 11 prep sessions. The punter likely sustained his groin injury in the Dolphins' Week 10 loss to the Colts. Jack Browning is set to be elevated from the practice squad ahead of Sunday's game against the Bills to take over punting duties.

Brewer was unable to play against the Colts in Week 10 while in the league's concussion protocol. He logged a full practice Friday, but he won't be allowed to suit up Sunday unless he passes an evaluation by an independent neurologist, which would get him out of protocol. Andrew Meyer would likely start at center if Brewer is not available.

Wayne will miss a second straight game due to a quadriceps injury, and his next chance to suit up is Week 12 against the Jets on Sunday, Nov. 29. In his absence, Kevin Coleman and Jalen Tolbert will serve as the Dolphins' rotational wide receivers behind Malik Washington, Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell.

Trader opened the week as a non-participant in practice after suffering groin and shoulder injuries during the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts last Sunday. Kyle Louis and Julius Wood may see more time in his place if Trader does indeed miss Week 11. Trader has 45 tackles (23 solo) and three pass breakups, including one interception, through nine 2026 regular-season games.

Phillips was recently placed on injured reserve with a season-ending biceps injury sustained in Week 10 versus the Colts. The 22-year-old ends his season with 28 tackles (11 solo) through nine games. Kenneth Grant and Keith Cooper are top candidates to see more reps at defensive tackle as the season continues.

Biggers suffered a lateral meniscus tear in Week 10, and he will now miss the remainder of the 2026 campaign while on IR. Fellow defensive lineman Jordan Phillips (biceps) was also placed on IR on Tuesday, and as a result, Kenneth Grant will operate as the team's top dog at defensive tackle moving forward this season.

Minnesota Vikings.longComment: Rodgers popped up on Thursday's practice report as a limited participant due to a quad injury. His practice reps were also limited in Friday's session, and his status for Sunday's contest may not be officially known until the Vikings announce their list of inactive players approximately 90 minutes before the 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff. Rookie fifth-rounder Charles Demmings and Zemaiah Vaughn would likely be the top candidates to start opposite James Pierre if Rodgers is not cleared to play against San Francisco.

The quarterback lost his job to Kirk Cousins and will continue to manage a hamstring injury. Murray's availability will only matter moving forward if something happens to Cousins, either performance or injury related. Carson Wentz and Max Brosmer remain on the 53-man roster as backup options.

Richter will now be forced to miss at least four games after suffering a foot injury during the Week 10 win over the Packers. The 26-year-old has compiled six tackles (three solo) across nine appearances this season while playing almost exclusively on special teams.

Thus, the Vikings are expecting Addison to recover fully before the four games required of an IR stint, but in any case he will miss some time due to the thumb injury he suffered in practice last Friday and sidelined him this past Sunday at Green Bay. With Addison out of the lineup, Minnesota will be relying on Justin Jefferson, Jauan Jennings (calf), Myles Price, Tai Felton and Jeshaun Jones at wide receiver.

New England Patriots.longComment: New England's trade for Brown is going down as one the team would definitely prefer to reverse. He's shown no chemistry with Drake Maye (ankle) and hasn't looked healthy since injuring his ankle in the first half of the Week 1 game against the Seahawks. Brown also appears to have lost multiple steps with his downfield speed due to the laundry list of lower-body injuries that now includes ankle, knee and hamstring issues in 2026. The Patriots will play out the string on a lost season without Maye and Brown for several more weeks. Look for Mack Hollins, Romeo Doubs (shoulder, IR) when healthy, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism to pick up the slack at wideout with Brown on the shelf again.

Maye was knocked out of Week 10 action on the first possession of this past Sunday's loss to the Lions in Munich. He already was expected to miss multiple games as a result of the injury, but with a diagnosis now available, he's now in rehab mode until further notice. A return at some point down the stretch likely will depend on the Patriots remaining in the playoff race, but for the time being Tommy DeVito will be under center in place of Maye.

Jones left the game during the fourth quarter, and given the score of the contest, the veteran linebacker is unlikely to return to Sunday's game. If that's the case, then Jones will finish with two tackles (one solo) and one QB hit.

Spillane went to the locker room in the third quarter, and he's being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's international game. Darius Muasau has taken over for Spillane at inside linebacker.

New Orleans Saints.longComment: Richards suffered a significant knee injury in the Saints' Week 10 loss to the Panthers. The offensive tackle is expected to miss multiple weeks due to the injury, so his absence for Week 11 is no surprise. Mason Murphy is set to start at right tackle while Richards recovers.

McCoy has not practiced since sustaining a biceps injury in the Saints' Week 9 clash with the Browns. The center will now miss consecutive games due to the injury, leaving Cesar Ruiz to start at center against the Bears.
Fuaga did not participate in any Week 11 prep sessions due to a knee injury he sustained during Week 10 prep. The right tackle will now miss consecutive games due to the issue.

Emerson was unable to practice all week while in the league's concussion protocol. The fifth-year defensive back will not suit up for Sunday's contest, so Quincy Riley figures to be the top candidate to start at outside cornerback opposite Kool-Aid McKinstry in the absence of Emerson, whose next chance to play is Week 12 against the Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Werner was held out of practice all week while managing a hamstring injury that he sustained against the Panthers in Week 10. Despite the lack of practice reps, the sixth-year pro has drawn the questionable tag for Sunday's road contest. Danny Stutsman would likely start at inside linebacker next to Kaden Elliss if Werner is unable to play against Chicago.

Miller is dealing with a knee injury and is now required to miss at least four games. The rookie nose tackle has played in four games this season, logging five tackles (two solo) over 93 snaps on defense and four snaps on special teams. Nathan Shepherd and Khristian Boyd could both get more defensive snaps during Miller's absence.

New York Giants.longComment: The Giants haven't provided any updates on Tracy since he landed on IR on Oct. 27 after sustaining a hamstring strain in a Week 7 win over the Texans, but the running back is seemingly progressing well and could be ready to play once he sits out the required four games. Once he's reinstated, Tracy could operate as a change-of-pace option behind Cam Skattebo, who appears to have reclaimed the lead role out of the New York backfield after a one-game benching in Week 6.

New York Jets.longComment: Parham practiced in all three Week 11 prep sessions, logging consecutive limited practices before upgrading to a full participant Friday. Despite the upgrade to full participation, the offensive guard remains questionable for Sunday's contest, meaning his knee is likely still bothering him.

Phillips started Week 11 prep as a DNP before logging consecutive limited sessions to end the week. If the defensive tackle is unable to suit up for Sunday's contest, Jack Heflin and Payton Page may see more rotational defensive snaps behind Darrell Jackson and Jowon Briggs.

Onyemata was designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday and strung together three consecutive limited practice sessions. However, the veteran defensive tackle is not quite ready to come off IR, so his next chance to play is Week 12 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 29. Onyemata has not played since Week 2 against the Packers due to an abdominal injury.

A groin injury has prevented Wallace from playing in each of the Jets' last two games. He's questionable for Sunday's road game, but his ability to practice in full Friday indicates that the third-year linebacker is trending in the right direction heading into the weekend.

With Omar Cooper (ankle/hip) also slated to be unavailable for the contest, Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell will lead the Jets' Week 11 WR corps, with coach Aaron Glenn noting Friday that the team's tight ends, primarily Kenyon Sadiq and Mason Taylor, should have an opportunity to see added opportunities as pass catchers this weekend in the absence of both Cooper and Williams.

Cooper didn't practice Wednesday or Thursday due to a pair of injuries, and he'll wind up sitting out Week 11. Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell will be the primary wideouts for the Jets, and with Isaiah Williams (ribs) joining Cooper on the sidelines, Malik McClain and Tim Patrick will be options when the team wants to get more receivers on the field, and per head coach Aaron Glenn -- via Rich Cimini of ESPN.com -- Sterling Shepard and tight ends Kenyon Sadiq and Mason Taylor could also get involved.

Philadelphia Eagles.longComment: Wicks missed the three games before the Eagles' Week 10 bye due to an ankle injury, and he was limited during Week 11 prep before the team tacked on a foot issue on Friday's practice report, after which he was ruled out for Sunday's contest against the Steelers. His placement on IR means he'll be sidelined until at least Saturday, Nov. 19, against the Seahawks.

Despite the extra rest courtesy of the Week 10 bye, Baun was not cleared to practice during Week 11 prep due to a back injury that he sustained in Week 9 against the Giants. Smael Mondon (ankle) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's contest, so Jeremiah Trotter will likely start alongside Jihaad Campbell at inside linebacker. Baun's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Cowboys on Thanksgiving Day.

Pittsburgh Steelers.longComment: Pittman was able to practice fully both Thursday and Friday, but he is not ready to rejoin the mix just yet -- which Pittsburgh confirmed by omitting Pittman from the list of roster moves they made Saturday. Barring an unannounced setback, Pittman figures to continue practicing, and his next chance to take the field will arrive on Black Friday when the Steelers square off against the Broncos.

Wilson has missed the Steelers' last four games while on injured reserve due to a left hand injury. He's still listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Eagles, but his activation from IR indicates that the third-year wide receiver will suit up for the Steelers. Michael Pittman (foot) is staying on IR for at least one more week, so as it stands, Wilson slots in as the team's WR3 behind DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard.

A hip injury prevented Herbig from participating in any of the Steelers' three practice sessions during Week 11 prep. The door was left ajar for him to play Sunday, but he'll observe the game from the sidelines, and his absence means Jack Sawyer will operate in an elevated role at edge rusher behind starters Alex Highsmith and T.J. Watt. Herbig's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Broncos on Friday.

Elliott was able to string together back-to-back full practices to end Week 11 prep, which is an encouraging sign despite the questionable tag. His official status for Sunday's game may not be known until about 90 minutes before the 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff, when the Steelers announce their list of inactive players. Robert Spears-Jennings and Brandin Echols would be the top candidates to start alongside Jaquan Brisker at safety if Elliott is not cleared by medical staff to play against the Eagles.

Queen put together an LP-LP-FP practice log during Week 11 prep, and despite the full session Friday, the veteran linebacker has been given the questionable tag for Sunday's game. If Queen cannot play against Philadelphia, then Cole Holcomb would likely start at inside linebacker alongside Payton Wilson, with Carson Bruener providing depth at the position.

Dunker went to IR with a sprained MCL back in late September, but it now looks like he's close to being available again. The move opens a 21-day window during which Pittsburgh can officially activate him before he'd have to go back on the shelf for the remainder of the campaign.

McCormick dislocated his ankle during the Steelers' 38-18 loss to the Bengals on Sunday. The good news for the third-year pro is that he avoided a fracture and does not require surgery, so there's a chance he could return for the Steelers should the team qualify for the playoffs, per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. Brock Hoffman figures to start at left guard in McCormick's stead.

San Francisco 49ers.longComment: West logged a trio of full practices during Week 11 prep, but he would need to be activated from injured reserve in order to be available for Sunday's game. He hasn't played since Week 2 against the Dolphins due to a knee injury, and his return would bolster the 49ers' depth at defensive tackle behind DeForest Buckner and Osa Odighizuwa.

Hobbs -- who opened the regular season on injured reserve due to a groin injury -- was a full participant in all three practices during Week 11 prep. However, he would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Sunday's contest. His return would give the 49ers extra depth at cornerback behind Deommodore Lenoir and Renardo Green, although Hobbs could easily step into a starting role in the secondary.

Greenlaw was held out of Wednesday's practice due to a neck injury. He was a limited participant both Thursday and Friday, which was enough for him to draw the questionable tag for Sunday's contest. Garret Wallow and Luke Gifford (chest) would be the top candidates to start at linebacker if Greenlaw is not cleared to play against Minnesota.

James' practice reps were limited both Thursday and Friday due to a calf injury. He was limited to kickoff return duties against the Cowboys in Week 10, and that role could be taken over by Deebo Samuel and/or Jacob Cowing if James is unable to play Sunday.

Jones put together an LP-DNP-LP practice log while working through an illness, which puts him in jeopardy of not being available for Sunday's contest. If Jones is inactive, then Kurtis Rourke would operate as the 49ers' backup to Brock Purdy,

Evans got back on the practice field Thursday as a limited participant, marking his first on-field work since aggravating his right Achilles during a Week 6 win versus the Commanders. Shanahan indicated that the team wants to see how Evans reacts to this week's practices before making a call on his availability for Sunday's showdown. In the end, though, San Francisco may not make an official ruling on Evans' status until about 90 minutes before an 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff.

Guerendo has been on the PUP list with a pec injury since training camp, but it now looks like he may be making some progress toward returning to action. Even if he does get back to full strength at some point soon, though, it's not clear how much room there will be for him in a 49ers' backfield that has recently been dominated by veteran Christian McCaffrey and rookie third-rounder Kaelon Black.

After he had missed the 49ers' first six games of the season while recovering from a calf injury, Kirk landed on injured reserve for the second time this season back on Nov. 7 due to a right knee injury sustained in his team debut Week 7 in Atlanta. Since Kirk didn't specify whether he required a partial meniscectomy or a meniscus repair, his exact recovery timeline isn't known. Regardless, he'll have to miss at least two more games while he's on IR.

This is the first time Stribling has participated in on-field work since suffering a significant ankle injury in the Week 1 win over the Rams. The expectation has been that the rookie could be back by December, so Stribling is progressing toward hitting that goal. Once Stribling progresses to full-team drills, his timeline will get more dialed in. The 49ers have two more games in November, leaving the Week 13 matchup against the Giants as his earliest potential return date.

After Aiyuk filed his paperwork for reinstatement, San Francisco activated him from the reserve/left squad list Nov. 9. Rosenhaus noted that Aiyuk passed his physical at that time, with MRIs and X-rays on his surgically repaired knee revealing no concerns. The 49ers were granted a two-week roster exemption for Aiyuk that will expire next Monday, and the 28-year-old wideout is expected to be cut loose at that time since San Francisco seemingly hasn't expressed interested in retaining him. While it's unclear what kind of market might exist for Aiyuk's services coming off a lengthy layoff from NFL action, NFL reporter Jordan Schultz relayed earlier this month that at least one NFC team has expressed interest in adding the receiver to its practice squad.

Seattle Seahawks.longComment: Holani exited Sunday's Week 10 game against the Raiders after suffering a knee injury. The 26-year-old is not currently expected to be placed on injured reserve, but he will be reevaluated after Seattle's Week 11 bye. The three-year pro has had a larger role on special teams since Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price returned from injuries to helm Seattle's ground attack.

Darnold, who last played in Week 8, still is working his way through a pair of injuries, but barring any setbacks, he's trending toward a Week 12 return. Macdonald reiterated that Darnold will be the team's starter once healthy, even though backup Drew Lock has guided Seattle to a 4-0 record while coming on in relief or starting in place of an injured Darnold in the first two games of the season as well as the most recent two contests.

Reed limped off the field during the first half and was subsequently deemed doubtful to return. Brandon Pili should get a lot more defensive snaps in the likely scenario that Reed is unable to re-enter Sunday's contest.

Lucas exited the first quarter of Sunday's game with an ankle injury. The right tackle appears to have sustained a significant injury and likely will not return to the contest. Josh Jones should finish the game at right tackle for the Seahawks.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers.longComment: Hayes was a full participant in all three practice sessions during Week 11 prep, but he is not quite ready to return from a knee procedure that he underwent in late August. His next chance to play is Week 12 against the Panthers on Monday, Nov. 30.

Diaby suffered a Grade 2 MCL sprain during the Buccaneers' Week 8 win over the Falcons, and the injury prevented him from playing against the Bears in Week 9. He had additional time to recover thanks to the Buccaneers' Week 10 bye, and he drew the questionable tag for Sunday's game after putting together an LP-LP-FP practice log. Diaby's return would result in less defensive snaps for David Walker and Al-Quadin Muhammad.

Winfield injured his ankle against the Bears in Week 9, and the extra week of rest courtesy of the bye was not enough for him to practice in any capacity during Week 11 prep. Ifeatu Melifonwu will likely start alongside Tykee Smith at safety in the absence of Winfield, whose next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Panthers on Monday, Nov. 30.

While Bowles indicated that linebacker Yaya Diaby (knee) has decent odds of playing in the Buccaneers' next game Nov. 22 versus the Lions, the coach was less optimistic about McMillan's chances of being ready to play in Week 11. The Buccaneers have yet to open McMillan's 21-day practice window, after he was placed on injured reserve Sept. 30 due to a PCL sprain in his left knee, which was an aggravation of a previous injury. Bowles noted that McMillan underwent a medical procedure on the knee shortly after landing on IR and is still dealing with some discomfort.

Tennessee Titans.longComment: Spears was sidelined for Weeks 7 and 8 due to a knee injury but was cleared to play against the Jaguars in Week 10, when he turned four carries into 28 yards and failed to haul in his lone target. He was initially listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Cowboys after logging a full practice Friday, but the Titans have determined that a stint on injured reserve is warranted for the fourth-year running back. Spears will be required to miss at least the next four games, so his next chance to play is Week 15 against the Colts on Sunday, Dec. 20. Tony Pollard will continue to be the workhorse running back for the Titans while Julius Chestnut and rookie fifth-rounder Nicholas Singleton provide depth out of the backfield.

Tate drew the questionable tag for Week 11 after a full practice Friday, and all signs point toward the rookie fourth-overall pick returning from a two-game absence due to a shoulder injury. With Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle, IR) out for the rest of the year, Tate will lead a Titans wideout group that also includes Elic Ayomanor, Chimere Dike, Xavier Restrepo and Calvin Ridley. Tennessee faces a Dallas defense Sunday that ranks 26th in the NFL in passing yards allowed per game (239.7) and 30th in points allowed per game (28.2).

Even with the questionable tag, Hill's full practice Friday indicates that the rookie second-rounder is trending in the right direction in his recovery from a neck injury, which prevented him from playing against the Jaguars in Week 10. His return would further bolsters a Titans linebacker corps that will welcome back Cody Barton, who also missed Week 10 while in the league's concussion protocol. Dorian Mausi would likely start at linebacker if Hill is not cleared to play against Dallas.

Carmona returned to practice Wednesday as a limited participant in what was his first workout with the team since sustaining an ankle sprain in the Titans' Sept. 27 loss to the Giants. The Titans will have a 21-day window to evaluate him in practice, but once Carmona is deemed ready to return from IR, he could step into a starting role at either left or right guard.

Meanwhile Carnell Tate (shoulder) is slated to practice this week, and his potential return to action this weekend against Dallas figures to impact the playing time of Elic Ayomanor and Chimere Dike. Robinson's looming absence will free up snaps/targets in the slot, with Saleh noting Wednesday that he's looking forward to seeing what rookie slot option Xavier Restrepo can do with added opportunities going forward.

Washington Commanders.longComment: Croskey-Merritt logged a full week of practice since the Commanders designated him for return from injured reserve Tuesday, which generally is a good sign he'll return to action Monday. Meanwhile, fellow RB Rachaad White was limited Friday and didn't practice Saturday due to a heel issue, also leaving him questionable for Week 11 action. The team will need to activate Croskey-Merritt from IR by Monday afternoon for him to have a chance to suit up, and if that comes to pass, he may have to contend with only Austin Ekeler for touches if White is inhibited or sidelined.

White has been working through a heel injury, but head coach Dan Quinn told reporters Saturday that the fifth-year running back should be available to play. White has operated as the Commanders' RB1 over the team's last four games, but his role will likely shrink for Week 11 given that Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is expected to be activated off injured reserve ahead of Monday night's game.

Tunsil underwent surgery in August to repair a torn triceps. The left tackle continues to recover, but he likely will not suit up for the Commanders in 2026 unless the team makes a playoff run. Even then, it remains unclear whether Tunsil would be able to return at all before the 2027 season.

The Commanders have been managing Burks' practice reps, as he deals with a foot injury that's been nagging him for several weeks. He missed practice time last week but still was able to play against the Giants last Thursday, securing two of three targets for 27 yards. Washington will provide final injury designations Saturday ahead of Monday night's game against the Bengals.

Martin played only 34 of the Commanders' 65 defensive snaps in Week 10 against the Giants, and a shoulder injury might help to explain why. Unless he's able to upgrade to full participation at practice Friday or Saturday, it seems like he's on track to carry an injury designation when Washington releases its final injury report of the week ahead of Monday night's matchup against the Bengals.
